solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Consider changing gear on the road

indicators.note: on means the road abbreviation follows straight after the scrambled letters
changing tells us the letters of gear are switched into a new order

parts.note: RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A driver thinks about shifting gear while out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' tempts as the definition in a motoring surface, but it is only the fodder; 'on' places the road abbreviation after the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it and weigh it up, a plain synonym of consider.

clue.text: Distribute or secure aid

indicators.note: distribute means spread around, so the letters of the next two words are shared out afresh

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand out or guarantee assistance to those in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribute' looks like the definition beside 'aid', but it is the anagram signal working on OR SECURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a source of help or supply that one can draw on, so it means aid.

clue.text: Swift traveller

parts.note: not a fast-moving tourist but the travelling hero created by Jonathan Swift in his satire of voyages to Lilliput

explanation.surface: Someone who gets about very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemuel Gulliver is the voyaging narrator of Jonathan Swift's famous satirical novel.

clue.text: It is a swindle to put a penny on farm butter

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another places it beneath, so the penny comes after

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so on a farm it is a butter

explanation.surface: A farmer is accused of cheating by charging an extra penny for butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farm butter' reads as dairy produce but means an animal that butts: a RAM. RAMP is an old word for a con or racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket, especially one that pushes prices up unfairly.

clue.text: A diet put out for fitness

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these three words are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone puts a diet into action in pursuit of physical fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitness' tempts as gym fitness, but here it means suitability or natural ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitude is a natural ability or suitability for something, the sense of fitness meaning being fit for a task.

clue.text: Nearest point at sea for the launch

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship is launched at the nearest point offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical surface makes 'launch' look like a boat; it is the unveiling of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: A product launch is a public presentation where something new is shown off for the first time.

clue.text: A preposition — one not out of order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: out of order means the letters of not are disarranged

explanation.surface: A grammar remark that a certain small word is not being used wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A preposition' is a fair if bare definition by category; 'out of order' signals the anagram, and the rearranged letters follow the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a preposition expressing motion towards the inside of something, as in walk into a room.

clue.text: Straighten things out and become more friendly

definitions.meaning: to straighten something bent is to take the bend out of it
to relax and become less stiff or formal in manner

explanation.definitionFit: Unbend literally means to straighten what was bent and figuratively to relax one's reserve.

clue.text: The son most likely to succeed?

definitions.text: The son most likely to succeed?

parts.words: The son most likely to succeed?
parts.note: succeed here means inherit the title or estate, which by primogeniture goes to the firstborn son

explanation.surface: Which boy in a family seems destined for success in life?
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest son is first in line to inherit, so most likely to succeed his father.

clue.text: Head dancer?

parts.note: not the leading ballerina but the biblical dancer who demanded John the Baptist's head as her reward

explanation.surface: Who is the principal dancer in the company?
explanation.definitionFit: Salome danced for Herod and asked for the head of John the Baptist on a platter.

clue.text: Passing place

parts.note: not a lay-by on a narrow road but where someone passes away, meaning dies

explanation.surface: A spot on a single-track road where cars can pull in to let others by.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathbed is the bed where a person dies, passing being a euphemism for death.

clue.text: Supporters of wicked things

parts.note: wicked here means having a wick, so the things supported are lit tapers rather than evil deeds

explanation.surface: People who back evil causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlesticks are holders that support candles, the things that have wicks.

clue.text: One has a lot of fun with it

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so one letter of the word fun is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a great time with a certain thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' keeps most of FUN, losing its F to leave UN, then IT is joined on.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or quantity regarded as one whole.

clue.text: Has an inclination for debauched men

definitions.meaning: to slope or lean, as a stage or a ship's mast does
dissolute pleasure-seeking men, short for rakehells

explanation.definitionFit: Rakes is a verb meaning slopes at an angle and a plural noun for dissolute men.

clue.text: Where lies our responsibility

parts.note: the clue asks where a duty is placed, and the reply, a preposition followed by a first-person plural pronoun, is itself a word for a burden

explanation.surface: A question about where our duty truly rests.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, and read as two words it is one resting on us.

clue.text: Turn taps a quarter and get a flood

indicators.note: turn means the word taps is reversed

parts.note: E for East is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Turning the taps a quarter turn produces a gush of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses TAPS to SPAT. 'a quarter' looks like part of the turn but gives E, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood of a river, and by extension any rush of things.

clue.text: Meals provided for the directors

definitions.meaning: the governing body of a company

explanation.definitionFit: Board means daily meals provided, as in full board, and also a company's directors.

clue.text: Something bound to appeal to the less affluent readers

definitions.text: Something bound to appeal to the less affluent readers

parts.words: Something bound to appeal to the less affluent readers
parts.note: bound means given a binding, so this is a book printed at low cost for buyers with less money

explanation.surface: A thing certain to attract poorer readers of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap edition is a low-priced printing of a book aimed at buyers with little money.

clue.text: Governed, having been shown the way

explanation.definitionFit: Directed means both managed or controlled and given directions on how to get somewhere.

clue.text: Such ladies' shoes were impressive

parts.note: impressive here means leaving impressions, since the thin spiked heels famously dent floors

explanation.surface: A remark that a style of women's footwear made a strong impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiletto heels are narrow spiked heels notorious for leaving marks in floors.

clue.text: Way painter treats sitter in a different pose

indicators.note: a different pose means the letters of treats sitter are arranged another way

explanation.surface: An artist handles a model by asking for a change of position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way painter' means a painter on the street, not a painter with a certain method.
explanation.definitionFit: A street artist paints on pavements or walls, so a way painter is one working on a road.

clue.text: Disorder for a month on the border

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes first

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Unrest lasts a month along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means violent disorder or chaos.

clue.text: Change planes in Italy

definitions.note: the definition describes a city found in Italy

indicators.note: change means the letters of planes are altered in order

explanation.surface: A traveller switches flights at an Italian airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large city in southern Italy, so this describes a place located in Italy.

clue.text: Whaler's cry of surprise touches sailor

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as whaler is

indicators.note: touches means the two pieces meet side by side

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A whaling man's exclamation reaches a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab is the obsessive whaling captain in Melville's novel Moby-Dick.

clue.text: A seat to put in the sun

indicators.note: put in tells us the word to is placed inside the sun word

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to place a chair out in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple seat without back or arms.

clue.text: Strip off on the Manx shore

definitions.meaning: to remove the outer layer or skin of something
a town on the west coast of the Isle of Man, whose people and things are called Manx

explanation.walkthrough: PEEL is a fishing town on the Isle of Man's coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel means remove a skin and is also a coastal town on the Isle of Man.

clue.text: A row in the amphitheatre

parts.note: not a quarrel among spectators but one of the stepped rows of seats in an arena

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows of seats rising above one another.

clue.text: You wouldn't credit it!

parts.note: credit is taken in the accounting sense, so the thing described sits on the opposite side of the ledger

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, the opposite of a credit in accounts.

clue.text: Measure appropriate for East Enders

definitions.meaning: a small length of half of a standard imperial unit
appropriate means steal, which in Cockney rhyming slang is pinch, rhyming with this phrase

explanation.walkthrough: East Enders are Cockneys from London's East End; in their rhyming slang this phrase means pinch, which means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small length measurement and Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal or appropriate.

clue.text: Set of six texts put out around the East

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round another piece
put out means the letters of texts are disordered

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone sends out half a dozen text messages around the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' turns TEXTS into SEXTT, and 'around' places it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group or set of six, especially musicians.

clue.text: Suspicion of corrosion after condensation

indicators.note: after means the corrosion word follows the condensation word

parts.note: mist is a fine film of condensed water droplets
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Rust appears after damp has collected on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is a lack of trust, closely matching suspicion.

clue.text: I ring boss before arriving at the work-room

indicators.note: before tells us the boss word comes ahead of the other two pieces

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone phones their manager before reaching the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I ring boss' reads as a phone call, but ring is O and boss a STUD, which goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist or craftsman works.
